dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a regular 2,800 ppm dip every 1.14 days on the M dwarf that is flat-bottomed, 1.9 Earth radii and seen in 37 transits with no odd/even or secondary eclipses. Centroid imaging puts the source on the target and rules out nearby blended stars. The star rotates at essentially the same period with strong spot variability, which need more RVs to confirm the planet, but the dip itself is best explained as an ultra-short-period planet.
